constraint_decided_it: E12(x) => E11(x): E12 Production is a subclass of E11 Modification, and both E11's and E12's scope notes say an event 'should ALSO be documented using an instance of E81 Transformation' -- additively, not instead. The standard's own examples enforce the dual instantiation: E11 lists 'the transformation of the Enola Gay into a museum exhibit ... (E12, E81)' and E81 lists 'the mummification of Tut-Ankh-Amun (E81, E12)'. A rejects E11 outright as 'excluded by its own scope note', which the scope note does not say; B keeps the (E81, E12) pairing the CRM prescribes for a deliberate human production like the seamstress's recutting.
better_modelling: One event instance multiply instantiated as E81 Transformation AND E12 Production (per E81's Tut-Ankh-Amun and Venetian Loggia examples). P124 transformed -> the 1920s wedding gown (E22, ceases to exist as a unit of documentation); P123 resulted in -> the christening gown (E22); AND P108 has produced -> the christening gown, which the adopted 7.1.3 examples add explicitly ('[AND: has produced (P108) the City Hall of Heraklion (E22)]'). Neither answer asserts P108, the more specific E12-level property; both stop at the P92 subproperty P123. Domain/range hold throughout: P123/P124 are E81 -> E18 and E22 is a subclass of E18.
reasoning: Both answers reach the same headline modelling and it is the right one: E81's scope note requires simultaneous destruction and creation preserving recognizable substance and structure with 'fundamentally different nature or identity', which the discarded skirt and recut panels satisfy, and P123/P124 (E81 -> E18) hold for E22. A's four quotations all verify verbatim (crm732#E11, issue12#current-s0000 x2, issue287#outcome) and Issue 287's outcome genuinely says 'E81 Transformation is certainly better than E11 Modification', so nothing in A is unsupported -- but A then over-reads 'should also be documented' as exclusion and rejects E11 wholesale, which contradicts E11's own '(E12, E81)' Enola Gay example and drops the E12 Production aspect of a deliberately produced garment. B recovers that aspect and its mummification precedent is real (E81 example, and t1396 msg 6: Doerr, 'multiclass examples are intrinsic to the whole idea of transformation'), though B repeats the same 'rather than E11/E12' misreading and, like A, omits P108 has produced, so it too is short of the fullest prescribed modelling.
